claims.text: The initial material is an as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy-alloy thin film.
The initial film has an ordered, single-phase hexagonal structure.
The initial film has minimal intrinsic strain.
Epitaxial strain modulates the energy landscape of the alloy's first-order magnetostructural transition.
Epitaxial strain can reduce transition hysteresis.
Epitaxial strain can shift the magnetostructural transition temperature.
The strain-induced changes can preserve a large magnetocaloric entropy change.
Pulsed-laser deposition on MgO can produce an epitaxial thin film.
Varying substrate lattice parameters can impose controlled tensile or compressive strain on the FeMnNiGeSi-type film.
An intervening buffer layer can mitigate extrinsic film-substrate interfacial artifacts.
The relevant controlled strain range is approximately -2% to +2%.
The magnetic-cooling cycles are to be conducted near the transition under applied fields up to approximately 0.1 T.
Substrate-induced strain distorts the lattice, changing unit-cell volume and local bond angles.
Changes in lattice parameters and bond angles alter the energy barrier and kinetics of the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Altered transition barriers and kinetics produce a smoother and less hysteretic transformation.
Optimally strained films will show a measurable transition-temperature shift and a statistically significant hysteresis reduction relative to unstrained or polycrystalline controls.
Buffer-layer controls can distinguish strain effects from extrinsic film-substrate interfacial effects.
The baseline has a sharp, hysteretic magnetostructural transition, a large entropy change, and limited reversibility during magnetic-cooling cycles.
The predicted behavior is expected only for epitaxial films under moderate strains of approximately -2% to +2%, and behavior outside that range may differ.
A lack of correlation between measured strain and both transition-temperature shifts and hysteresis reduction would falsify the strain-mediated explanation.
